contentObjective: I can write equivalent fractions, decimals, and percents for the same value.

vocabulary.definition: Three equivalent ways to name the same part of a whole.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Tres maneras equivalentes de nombrar la misma parte de un todo.
vocabulary.cloze: Three equivalent ways to name the same part of a whole are ___, ___ and ___.

examples.why: All three name the same amount of the same whole.
0.2 is a different amount, so the set is not equivalent.

vocabulary.definition: A way to compare a number to 100, shown with the % sign.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una manera de comparar un número con 100, con el signo %.
vocabulary.cloze: A ratio that compares a number to 100, written with a % sign, is a ___.

examples.text: 9 out of 100 students walk to school → 9%
examples.why: The comparison is already out of 100.
That is 90%, not 9% — both terms must be scaled to 100.

vocabulary.definition: A number with a dot, like 0.5, that shows a part less than one.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número con un punto, como 0.5, que muestra una parte menor que uno.
vocabulary.cloze: A number that uses a point to show parts of a whole is a ___.

examples.why: The percent divided by 100 gives the decimal.
Multiplying by a plain 35 makes the answer 100 times too big.

vocabulary.definition: Having the same value, just written a different way.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Tener el mismo valor, escrito de otra forma.
vocabulary.cloze: Having the same value but written a different way is being ___.

vocabulary.definition: A familiar number you use to guess, like 50% or 1/2.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número conocido que usas para estimar, como 50% o 1/2.
vocabulary.cloze: A common, easy-to-remember value like 50% or 1/4 used for comparing is a ___.

examples.text: Using 25% of 80 to check a 24% discount
examples.why: A friendly percent close enough to estimate with.
Those are the exact numbers — that is computing, not benchmarking.

vocabulary.definition: Money taken off the first price to make it cheaper.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dinero que se quita del precio original para que sea más barato.
vocabulary.cloze: An amount taken off a price, often given as a percent, is a ___.

examples.why: Money taken off the original price.

examples.text: The $60 you pay at the register
examples.why: That is the sale price — what is left after the discount.

vocabulary.definition: The second place after the decimal point; parts out of 100.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La segunda posición después del punto decimal; partes de 100.
vocabulary.cloze: The decimal place that shows parts out of 100 is the ___ place.

examples.why: It is two places after the point.
It is one place after the point, so it is tenths.

vocabulary.definition: One form, such as percents, that every value in a list is rewritten in.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una forma, como porcentajes, en la que se reescriben todos los valores de una lista.
vocabulary.visual: All written as percents before ordering.
vocabulary.cloze: Rewriting every value the same way puts them in a ___.

examples.why: Every value is now a percent.
The values are still in three different forms.

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Sleepy Animals
revealWordProblem.text:
The table shows the average total sleep time for different animals as a part of a 24-hour day. Some are written as decimals, some as fractions, and some as percents.
Question: How do the sleep times compare? Order the animals from the one that sleeps the most to the one that sleeps the least. Which animal's sleep time surprised you, and why?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A table of average sleep time as part of a 24-hour day for eight animals, written as a mix of decimals, fractions, and percents.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Rewrite every value in the same form — decimals are easiest. Python 3/4 = 0.75, Tiger 0.65, Cheetah 0.5, Duck 0.45, Chimpanzee 2/5 = 0.4, Human 33% = 0.33, Cow 16.5% = 0.165, Giraffe 8/100 = 0.08. From most to least: python, tiger, cheetah, duck, chimpanzee, human, cow, giraffe. The giraffe is the surprise — 0.08 of a day is only about 2 hours of sleep, while the python sleeps about 18.

choiceFeedback: Try again: 5 × 20 = 100, so multiply the top by 20 as well.
Build an equivalent fraction with denominator 100 — multiply the top and bottom by the same number.
hints: Percent means out of 100. What do you multiply the denominator 5 by to get 100?
5 × 20 = 100, so multiply the numerator by that same 20 to build the equivalent fraction.
3 × 20 = 60, so 3/5 = 60/100. A fraction out of 100 IS the percent.
hintsEs: Porcentaje significa de cada 100. ¿Por cuánto multiplicas el denominador 5 para llegar a 100?
5 × 20 = 100, así que multiplica el numerador por ese mismo 20 para formar la fracción equivalente.
3 × 20 = 60, entonces 3/5 = 60/100. Una fracción de cada 100 ES el porcentaje.

choiceFeedback: Scale 7/20 up to a denominator of 100 first.
Double-check: 20 × 5 = 100, so the top must be multiplied by 5 too.
hints: The denominator 20 is friendly: 20 × 5 = 100, and percents are always 'out of 100'.
Make an equivalent fraction with denominator 100 by multiplying top AND bottom by the same number.
Multiply 7/20 by 5/5: the bottom becomes 100. Whatever the top becomes is your percent.
hintsEs: El denominador 20 es amigable: 20 × 5 = 100, y los porcentajes siempre son 'de cada 100'.
Forma una fracción equivalente con denominador 100 multiplicando arriba Y abajo por el mismo número.
Multiplica 7/20 por 5/5: la parte de abajo se vuelve 100. Lo que quede arriba es tu porcentaje.

questions.explanation: 45% means 45/100, and 45/100 written as a decimal is 0.45 (forty-five hundredths).
choiceFeedback: 0.045 is forty-five THOUSANDTHS — one place too far. Percent to decimal moves the point exactly two places left.
Divide the percent by 100, or move the decimal point left 2 places.
45.0 keeps the percent's full size. Percent means 'per hundred,' so the decimal form must be much smaller — move the point two places left.
hints: Percent means 'out of 100', so 45% is the fraction 45/100.
To turn a percent into a decimal, divide by 100 — the decimal point slides two places to the LEFT.
Start at 45. and move the decimal two places left: 45 → 4.5 → where does it land after the second hop?
questions.explanationEs: 45% significa 45/100, y 45/100 escrito como decimal es 0.45 (cuarenta y cinco centésimos).
hintsEs: Porcentaje significa 'de cada 100', así que 45% es la fracción 45/100.
Para convertir un porcentaje en decimal, divide entre 100: el punto decimal se desliza dos lugares a la IZQUIERDA.
Empieza en 45. y mueve el punto dos lugares a la izquierda: 45 → 4.5 → ¿dónde cae después del segundo salto?

steps: 1. Percent to Decimal: Divide by 100 (move decimal point 2 places left)
2. Decimal to Percent: Multiply by 100 (move decimal point 2 places right)
3. Fraction to Percent: Divide numerator by denominator, then convert decimal to percent
reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Relate Fractions, Decimals, and Percents is treating the numerator and denominator as the percent's digits — turning 3/5 into "35%" by just reading the 3 and the 5. Percent means out of 100, so the fix is to build an equivalent fraction with denominator 100: 5 × 20 = 100, so multiply the top by 20 too — 3/5 = 60/100 = 60%. A second version of this mistake is scaling only ONE part of the fraction (writing 3/5 = 3/100 or 60/5). Whatever you multiply the denominator by, you must multiply the numerator by the same number. When a denominator will not reach 100 evenly (8, 3, 7), divide the numerator by the denominator instead and then multiply by 100.

hints: 2 × 50 = 100. Multiply the numerator by 50 too.
hintsEs: 2 × 50 = 100. Multiplica también el numerador por 50.
level1.explanation: Multiply the top and bottom by 50: 1/2 = 50/100 Write the decimal and the percent: 50/100 = 0.5 → 50%
level1.explanationEs: Multiplica el numerador y el denominador por 50: 1/2 = 50/100 Escribe el decimal y el porcentaje: 50/100 = 0.5 → 50%

hints: 5 × 20 = 100. Make a fraction out of 100 first.
hintsEs: 5 × 20 = 100. Primero forma una fracción de cada 100.
level1.explanation: Multiply the top and bottom by 20: 4/5 = 80/100 Write the hundredths as a decimal: 80/100 = 0.80 = 0.8
level1.explanationEs: Multiplica el numerador y el denominador por 20: 4/5 = 80/100 Escribe las centésimas como decimal: 80/100 = 0.80 = 0.8

hints: 20 × 5 = 100. Multiply the numerator by 5 too.
hintsEs: 20 × 5 = 100. Multiplica también el numerador por 5.
level1.explanation: Multiply the top and bottom by 5: 7/20 = 35/100 Read the percent: 35/100 → 35%
level1.explanationEs: Multiplica el numerador y el denominador por 5: 7/20 = 35/100 Lee el porcentaje: 35/100 → 35%

hints: Multiply the top and bottom by 10 to get a denominator of 100.
hintsEs: Multiplica el numerador y el denominador por 10 para tener un denominador de 100.
level1.explanation: Multiply the top and bottom by 10: 7/10 = 70/100 Read the percent from the numerator: 70/100 → 70%
level1.explanationEs: Multiplica el numerador y el denominador por 10: 7/10 = 70/100 Lee el porcentaje en el numerador: 70/100 → 70%

hints: First make an equivalent fraction out of 100. 25 × 4 = 100.
hintsEs: Primero forma una fracción equivalente de cada 100. 25 × 4 = 100.
level1.explanation: Multiply the top and bottom by 4: 3/25 = 12/100 Write the hundredths as a decimal: 12/100 = 0.12
level1.explanationEs: Multiplica el numerador y el denominador por 4: 3/25 = 12/100 Escribe las centésimas como decimal: 12/100 = 0.12

level2.stem: Ben says 0.6 is the same as 6%. Is he right? Write 0.6 as a percent.
level2.stemEs: Ben dice que 0.6 es lo mismo que 6%. ¿Tiene razón? Escribe 0.6 como porcentaje.
hints: Write 0.6 as hundredths first. 0.6 is 6 tenths.
hintsEs: Primero escribe 0.6 en centésimas. 0.6 es 6 décimos.
level2.explanation: Write 0.6 as hundredths: 0.6 = 0.60 = 60/100 Read the percent: 60/100 → 60%
level2.explanationEs: Escribe 0.6 en centésimas: 0.6 = 0.60 = 60/100 Lee el porcentaje: 60/100 → 60%

hints: 100 ÷ 40 is not a whole number. Divide the numerator by the denominator.
hintsEs: 100 ÷ 40 no es un número entero. Divide el numerador entre el denominador.
level2.explanation: Divide the numerator by the denominator: 3 ÷ 40 = 0.075 Check with the percent: 0.075 × 100 = 7.5
level2.explanationEs: Divide el numerador entre el denominador: 3 ÷ 40 = 0.075 Comprueba con el porcentaje: 0.075 × 100 = 7.5

hints: 20 × 5 = 100. Multiply the numerator by 5 too.
hintsEs: 20 × 5 = 100. Multiplica también el numerador por 5.
level2.explanation: Multiply the top and bottom by 5: 11/20 = 55/100 Read the percent: 55/100 → 55%
level2.explanationEs: Multiplica el numerador y el denominador por 5: 11/20 = 55/100 Lee el porcentaje: 55/100 → 55%

level2.stem: A fraction with a denominator of 20 is equal to 35%. What is its numerator?
level2.stemEs: Una fracción con denominador 20 es igual a 35%. ¿Cuál es su numerador?
hints: Write 35% as a fraction out of 100. Then work backward to a denominator of 20.
hintsEs: Escribe 35% como una fracción de cada 100. Luego trabaja hacia atrás hasta un denominador de 20.
level2.explanation: Write the percent as a fraction: 35% → 35/100 Divide the top and bottom by 5: 35/100 = 7/20
level2.explanationEs: Escribe el porcentaje como fracción: 35% → 35/100 Divide el numerador y el denominador entre 5: 35/100 = 7/20

level2.stem: A shirt is 1/4 off the price. Write the discount as a percent.
level2.stemEs: Una camisa tiene 1/4 de descuento sobre el precio. Escribe el descuento como porcentaje.
hints: What do you multiply 4 by to get 100?
hintsEs: ¿Por cuánto multiplicas 4 para llegar a 100?
level2.explanation: Multiply the top and bottom by 25: 1/4 = 25/100 Read the percent: 25/100 → 25%
level2.explanationEs: Multiplica el numerador y el denominador por 25: 1/4 = 25/100 Lee el porcentaje: 25/100 → 25%

level3.stem: What is the fraction 7/20 written as a decimal and as a percent?
choiceFeedback: The decimal point is one place too far left. 7 divided by 20 is 0.35.
The decimal is right but the percent is not. 0.35 is 35 hundredths, so it is 35%.
That is 7/10, not 7/20. Scale to hundredths: 7/20 equals 35/100.

level3.stem: Lily says 1/4 is 0.4, because the 4 moves after the decimal point. Write 1/4 as a decimal.
level3.stemEs: Lily dice que 1/4 es 0.4, porque el 4 pasa después del punto decimal. Escribe 1/4 como decimal.
hints: A fraction bar means divide. Or scale 4 to 100.
hintsEs: La barra de fracción significa dividir. O escala 4 a 100.
level3.explanation: Multiply the top and bottom by 25: 1/4 = 25/100 Write the hundredths as a decimal: 25/100 = 0.25
level3.explanationEs: Multiplica el numerador y el denominador por 25: 1/4 = 25/100 Escribe las centésimas como decimal: 25/100 = 0.25

hints: Divide 5 by 16. Then multiply the decimal by 100.
hintsEs: Divide 5 entre 16. Luego multiplica el decimal por 100.
level3.explanation: Divide the numerator by the denominator: 5 ÷ 16 = 0.3125 Multiply the decimal by 100: 0.3125 × 100 = 31.25 Write the percent: 0.3125 → 31.25%
level3.explanationEs: Divide el numerador entre el denominador: 5 ÷ 16 = 0.3125 Multiplica el decimal por 100: 0.3125 × 100 = 31.25 Escribe el porcentaje: 0.3125 → 31.25%

level3.stem: A test has 30 questions. Rosa gets 27 of them right. What percent of the questions does she get right?
level3.stemEs: Un examen tiene 30 preguntas. Rosa acierta 27 de ellas. ¿Qué porcentaje de las preguntas acierta?
hints: Write the fraction 27/30. Simplify it, then scale to 100.
hintsEs: Escribe la fracción 27/30. Simplifícala y luego escala a 100.
level3.explanation: Write the fraction and simplify: 27/30 = 9/10 Scale to 100: 9/10 = 90/100 Read the percent: 90/100 → 90%
level3.explanationEs: Escribe la fracción y simplifica: 27/30 = 9/10 Escala a 100: 9/10 = 90/100 Lee el porcentaje: 90/100 → 90%

hints: Write all three as decimals. Then compare the digits place by place.
hintsEs: Escribe los tres como decimales. Luego compara los dígitos lugar por lugar.
level3.explanation: Write 5/12 as a decimal: 5 ÷ 12 ≈ 0.417 Write 41.5% as a decimal: 41.5 ÷ 100 = 0.415 Compare the three decimals: 0.415 < 0.417 < 0.42
level3.explanationEs: Escribe 5/12 como decimal: 5 ÷ 12 ≈ 0.417 Escribe 41.5% como decimal: 41.5 ÷ 100 = 0.415 Compara los tres decimales: 0.415 < 0.417 < 0.42
choiceFeedback: 5/12 is about 0.417. That is less than 0.42.
